messages:
dana: Hey team — since the canary rolled last night, our /v1/chat calls started returning intermittent 502s and big latency spikes (~5–10s). Example failing request id: req_c7f9a2b1. We thought we had the model pinned to "stable-1.0" but the response headers include "x-model: redwood-candidate-v2". Can we get help reproducing? Here's the curl we used:

```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: req_c7f9a2b1" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"stable-1.0","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<large-system-context>"},{"role":"user","content":"summarize the following..."}]}'
```

alice: Thanks — can you paste the exact X-Request-ID value from the failing response header (if different) and confirm whether the pin is account-wide or per-request? Also include the timestamp of the failure if you have it.

dana: Response had header `x-request-id: req_c7f9a2b1` and server sent `x-srv-id: srv-9090`. Failures started ~2026-03-16T02:09:12Z. We're routing through the hosted API even though we have Dedicated capacity. We set `model` in body on most calls but might be missing on a batch job.

bob: Can you reproduce with this minimal curl and upload the trace? Add `--trace-ascii` or `--dump-header` to capture the raw headers. Also try adding `X-Debug: true` to trigger debug bundle generation server-side. Example reproducer:

```bash
curl https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "X-Request-ID: repro_local_001" \n  -H "X-Debug: true" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-candidate-v2","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' \n  --trace-ascii repro_local_001.trace
```

carlos: FYI deploy events show canary `redwood-candidate-v2` rolled at 2026-03-16T01:40:00Z. If routing sent requests to canary and it started returning 5xxs, the router should fallback to stable. Do you see fallback traffic (x-fallback-to: stable) in the headers?

dana: We see some `x-fallback-to: stable` headers but not for every failing request. Roughly 15% of requests (long prompts + stream=true) hit 502/504. Shorter requests are fine. We also saw a single 401 earlier today during a key rotation window. No billing 402/403s.

bob: Streaming + long system context is a known stress path on the candidate — could be kv-cache growth or a kernel-level OOB. Please try repro with a longer prompt and streaming enabled. If you can upload the `repro_local_001.trace` and the raw response body to the debug uploader (https://uploads.redwood.internal/debug) we'll pull the server logs for `req_c7f9a2b1` and the `srv-9090` host.

Also as a quick mitigation, force the stable model per-request: set `{"model":"redwood-stable-1.0","stream":false}` or add header `X-Model-Pin: stable-1.0`. That should avoid candidate routing until we confirm.

carlos: @bob can you check routing policy logs for `req_c7f9a2b1`? I want timeline: ingress -> router decision -> target host -> error -> fallback decision. If fallback decision was skipped that's a bug.

bob: Pulling logs now. Reproduced locally with the provided pattern: when `stream=true` + >4k token prompt to `redwood-candidate-v2` I hit a consistent 502 and a kernel-level validation error referencing kv cache. Starting a canary rollback now while we dig in.

Deploy events:
```
[deploy-bot] 1778997600 deploy start redwood-candidate-v2 (canary)
[deploy-bot] 1778997900 deploy complete redwood-candidate-v2
```

bob: Temporary workarounds: 1) pin the model explicitly in the request body (see above). 2) disable streaming for affected workloads. 3) if you can't change client, set account-level routing override to prefer stable for your org (we can flip this from our side).

dana: OK I'm going to try the explicit pin and run the repro with `--trace-ascii`. I'll upload the trace to the URL and paste the upload id here. Thanks for the quick triage.

alice: Plan: dana uploads trace + raw response; support will monitor; eng will confirm rollback/patch; SRE to validate routing fallback logic and add an alert for fallback failures. Follow-up: please include any client SDK versions. :thumbsup:

dana: Upload complete: https://uploads.redwood.internal/debug/trace_repro_local_001.tar.gz (upload id: up_57b9). Reproducer curl output attached in tar.

bob: Got it, pulling bundle. Escalating to runtime team — tagging `@eng-runtime` and `@eng-sre`. We'll update this thread with root cause or rollback window. Thanks everyone.

carlos: I'll keep an eye on metrics and will confirm when the rollback is live.

alice: Closing the loop when we have root cause; for customers: recommend pin + disable streaming until patch.

dana: Thanks all — appreciate the help.
